#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# PreToolUse:Bash Safety Hook — Block Destructive Commands (v1.38.0)
# =============================================================================
# Blocks dangerous patterns and suggests safer alternatives.
# Exit 0 = allow, Exit 2 = block (stderr message fed back to agent).
#
# Cycle-111 (sprint-164, 2026-05-16) — ports Anthropic DCG public pattern
# set inline. Source: github.com/anthropics/destructive-command-guard
# Pattern port reference SHA: HEAD as of 2026-05-16 (no specific commit
# pin available — DCG ships rule packs, not single-file source).
# REVIEW-BY: 2026-08-16 — re-sync against upstream DCG every quarter.
#
# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — this hook must never fail closed.
# A grep or jq failure must result in exit 0 (allow), not an error.
#
# WHY fail-open (not fail-closed): A safety hook that crashes or encounters
# a parse error must NOT block the agent from operating. The alternative —
# fail-closed — would make jq/grep bugs into denial-of-service attacks
# against the agent. Fail-open with logging is the standard pattern for
# inline security hooks (cf. ModSecurity DetectionOnly mode).
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix)
#
# WHY GNU/BSD ERE (NOT strict POSIX): grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension not
# available on macOS/BSD or minimal containers. grep -E (Extended Regex)
# with `\s`, `\S`, `\b` extensions works on both GNU grep (Linux) and BSD
# grep (macOS Sonoma+). Strict-POSIX ERE (busybox without -E extensions)
# is NOT in scope per cycle-111 SDD §5.0 honest-scope decision.
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix; cycle-111 SDD §5.0)
#
# WHY single script for all patterns: NFR-5 single-file invariant. Multiple
# hooks would each read stdin, parse JSON, and run regex — multiplying
# latency per command. A single emit_block helper with sequential patterns
# is simpler and faster. (cycle-111 SDD §5/§6.)
#
# Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111 SDD §11): this hook is a fence
# against routine destructive-command mistakes by autonomous agents, NOT
# a hardened security boundary against intentional bypass. Known accepted
# bypass classes: newline statement separators, subshell wrapping
# (`bash -c '...'`, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing
# WHERE, jq absent from PATH. See SDD §11 for full table.
# Current executable limit examples and issue dispositions:
# docs/runbooks/hook-safety.md (#1047, #1245, #1088, #1031).
#
# cycle-125 FR-1 (2026-09-23) — precision pass against the fleet corpus
# (tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/, replayed by tests/unit/block-destructive-
# bash.bats). Relaxations, each on a positively established predicate:
# FR-2 cache/build vocabulary by last segment, bare names after a
# statement-initial `cd <temp>`, paths strictly below /tmp|/var/tmp|
# /private/tmp, `$TMPDIR/<name>` only with a real temp TMPDIR, a variable
# bound exactly once to `$(mktemp -d)`; FR-1.1 branches that are ancestors
# of main/master (offline `git merge-base`); FR-1.3 generated paths;
# FR-1.4/5/6 only when a SQL runner (psql, mysql, sqlite3, prisma, …) or an
# inline interpreter program (`python -c`, `node -e`) is in the command.
# ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (deliberately not relaxed):
#   * Remote payloads: `ssh host 'rm -rf /'`, `docker exec c rm -rf /data`,
#     `kubectl exec p -- rm -rf /` keep blocking. A scrub of quoted remote
#     payloads was withdrawn at design time (Flatline SKP-001) — the text
#     fence cannot tell a remote target from a local one, and the blast
#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
#
# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
# under a caller's `set -u`.
#
# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
# =============================================================================
_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'

# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
  case "$1" in
    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
  case "$1" in
    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# Command words the fence's own rules match.
_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
  case "$1" in
    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
  case "$1" in
    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
  n=${#s}
  _bdb_hd_tok=()
  while (( i < n )); do
    ch="${s:i:1}"
    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
      tok="$tok$ch"
      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
        q=""
      fi
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    case "$ch" in
      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '\')
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
      ' '|$'\t')
        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '#')
        (( have )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
        op=""
        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
        done
        i=$((i + ${#op}))
        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
        fi
        if (( have )); then
          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
            op="$tok$op"
          else
            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
          fi
          tok=""; have=0
        fi
        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
  return 0
}

# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
  _hd_up=""
  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
    _hd_up="$1"
  else
    return 1
  fi
  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
}

# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
# content (or cannot be judged).
_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
  case "$p" in
    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
  esac
  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
  b="${p##*/}"
  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
  else d="${PWD:-.}"
  fi
  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
  done
  IFS="$old_ifs"
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
_bdb_hd_member() {
  local -a toks argv
  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
  _hd_mcls=none
  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
    t="${toks[i]}"
    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
      case "$t" in
        *'<<<') return ;;
        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
          continue ;;
        *) return ;;
      esac
    fi
    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
  done
  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
  a0="${argv[0]}"
  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
    t="${argv[i]}"
    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
  done
  case "$a0" in
    cat)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
    tee)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -a|--append|-p) ;;
          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
        esac
      done ;;
    echo|printf)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
      done ;;
    gh)
      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
        *) return ;;
      esac
      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
          -*)
            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
              i=$((i + 1))
              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
            fi ;;
          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
        esac
      done
      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    git)
      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
        esac
      done
      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    br)
      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in

input.command: cd /workspace/pr; sed -n 420,900p head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh

content.content:
case "$t" in
          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
        esac
      done
      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    jq|yq)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
      done ;;
    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
    sed)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
             fi ;;
        esac
      done
      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    sort)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
          -k*|-t*) ;;
          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
        esac
      done ;;
    wc)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
      done ;;
    *) return ;;
  esac
  _hd_mcls=nonexec
}

# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
  local l="${1:-}" k last
  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0
  for ((k = 0; k < ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}; k++)); do
    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
    esac
  done
  (( ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
  last="${_bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}-1]}"
  case "$last" in '|'|'|&'|'&&'|'||') return 0 ;; esac
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
_bdb_hd_header() {
  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
  local -a tpipe mtoks
  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
  _hd_dests=()
  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
  tpipe=()
  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
    case "$t" in
      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
    esac
    tpipe[k]=$pipe
    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
  done
  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
    _hd_delim="$w"
  else
    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
  fi
  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
  local cls=nonexec
  k=0
  while (( k < nt )); do
    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
    mtoks=()
    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
    case "$_hd_mcls" in
      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
    esac
    k=$((k + 1))
  done
  _hd_cls="$cls"
}

# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
_bdb_hd_segword() {
  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
  while (( guard < 64 )); do
    guard=$((guard + 1))
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
    case "${s:0:1}" in
      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
    esac
    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
    s="${s:${#w}}"
    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
    case "$w" in
      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
        while :; do
          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
          case "$s" in
            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
            *) break ;;
          esac
        done
        continue ;;
    esac
    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
    return
  done
}

# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
  local k l t seg
  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
    if (( ! $3 )); then
      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
    fi
    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
    while :; do
      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
          _hd_full=1
          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_full=1
        fi
      fi
      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
    done
  done
}

# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
    start=0 pipe=0
    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
      # segment [start, j)
      own=0
      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
      if (( ! own )); then
        seg_has=0 cw=""
        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
        done
        if (( seg_has )); then
          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
          cw="$_hd_w"
          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
        fi
      fi
      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
      start=$((j + 1))
    done
  done
  return 1
}

# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
  _bdb_hd_class=none
  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
  text="${text%$'\n'}"
  _bdb_hd_L=()
  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
  i=0
  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
      out="$out$l"$'\n'
      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
      out="$out$l"$'\n'
      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
    found=-1
    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
    done
    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
    cls="$_hd_cls"
    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
    fi
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
      local -a dests
      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
          cls=interpreter; break
        fi
      done
    fi
    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
    out="$out$l"$'\n'
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
        out="$out$_hd_kept"
      fi
    else
      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
      out="$out$_hd_synth"
    fi
    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
    case "$cls" in
      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
    esac
    i=$((found + 1))
  done
  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
}

# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
}

# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r l; do
    case "$l" in
      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
    esac
    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
    fi
  done <<< "$content"
  return 0
}

# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
  local LC_ALL=C
  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
}
heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
  return 0
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# jq presence probe (SDD §6.5 — SKP-008 mitigation, not full fix).
# If jq is absent, the input parse on line ~120 returns empty → existing
# fail-open guard exits 0. v1.38.0 adds a one-shot stderr WARNING so the
# operator / agent sees the safety guard is disabled this session.
# Tracked as cycle-112 candidate (filesystem-marker variant for cross-
# invocation persistence; env-var doesn't propagate across hook subprocess
# invocations per Flatline SKP-002 round-3 finding).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-11 (skill-loop, 2026-07-06): HIGH-002 fix (BB review of PR #1176).
# Passes 2 & 8 introduced bash-4-only constructs into this fence (${x,,}
# case-folding, `mapfile`); pre-loop it was bash-3.2-portable (echo|grep -i).
# macOS ships bash 3.2. This guard runs BEFORE any bash-4 expansion executes
# (bash 3.2 defers ${,,} validation and the mapfile builtin lookup to runtime,
# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)

_bdb_re_tail="^[[:space:]]*(-m|--message|-d|--description|--body|--title)[[:space:]]+${_bdb_qval_perm}"

   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
   229	  else
   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}

   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
   243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
   244	impl_commit() {
   245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
   246	  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
   247	    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
   248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
   249	}

   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}

   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
   281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
   282	      .cycle += 1
   283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
   284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
   285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
   286	      | .lc = $c);
   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
   288	  {state: "CLOSED",
   289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
   290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
   291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
   292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   293	   history: []};
   294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
   295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
   297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
   298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
   299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
   300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
   301	     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
   302	          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
   303	  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
   304	        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
   305	      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
   306	        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   307	      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
   308	        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   309	      else null end ) as $trip
   310	  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
   311	    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
   312	    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
   313	def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
   314	def resolve($f; $now; $win):
   315	  . as $c
   316	  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
   317	  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
   318	  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
   319	  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
   320	      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
   321	      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
   322	  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
   323	  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
   324	    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
   325	    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
   326	    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
   327	    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
   328	    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
   329	'

   331	cmd_derive() {
   332	  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
   333	  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   334	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
   335	  fi
   336	  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
   337	  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   338	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
   339	  fi
   340	  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
   341	  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))

   344	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
   345	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
   346	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
   347	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
   348	  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
   349	
   350	  # Per-sprint facts
   351	  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
   352	  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
   353	    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
   354	    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
   355	    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
   356	    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
   357	       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
   358	        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
   359	    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
   360	    | @tsv' "$ledger")
   361	  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
   362	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
   363	    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
   364	    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
   365	    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
   366	    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
   367	    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
   368	    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
   369	    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
   370	    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
   371	    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
   372	    mex=false; msid=""
   373	    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
   374	      mex=true
   375	      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
   376	    fi
   377	    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
   378	    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
   379	              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
   380	      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
   381	      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
   382	      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
   383	      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
   384	      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
   385	      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
   386	      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
   387	      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
   388	      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
   389	      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
   390	       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
   391	       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
   392	       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
   393	       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
   394	                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
   395	       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
   396	       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
   397	               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
   398	    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")

   400	
   401	  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
   402	  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
   403	  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
   404	  rounds="[]"

   413	  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
   414	  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
   415	
   416	  local facts report
   417	  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
   418	    {sprints: $s,
   419	     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
   420	     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
   421	     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
   422	     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
   423	     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
   424	  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
   425	                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
   426	                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
   427	    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
   428	    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
   429	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
   430	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
   431	    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
   432	       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
   433	       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
   434	       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
   435	       notes: ([
   436	         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
   437	         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
   438	         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
   439	         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
   440	         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
   441	       ]),
   442	       sprints: $f.sprints,
   443	       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
   444	       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
   445	                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
   446	       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
   447	       written: false}')
   448	
   449	  if (( write )); then
   450	    local why=""
   451	    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
   452	    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring

    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
   118	    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
   119	    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
   120	    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
   122	    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
   123	    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
   124	    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
   125	    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
   126	    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
   127	    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
   128	    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
   129	     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
   130	     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
   131	    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
   132	    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
   133	        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
   134	        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
   135	        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
   136	        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
   137	        else . end)) as $knobs |
   138	    {
   139	      schema_version: 1,
   140	      id: $id,
   141	      profile: $sel.name,
   142	      profile_source: $sel.source,
   143	      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
   144	      profile_keys: $keys,
   145	      knobs: $knobs,
   146	      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
   147	                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
   148	                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
   149	      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
   150	                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
   151	    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
   152	  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
   153	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
   154	    return 1
   155	  fi
   156	  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
   157	  local w
   158	  while IFS= read -r w; do
   159	    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
   160	  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
   161	  return 0
   162	}
   163	
   164	_loa_pl_write_cache() {
   165	  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
   166	  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
   167	  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
   168	  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
   169	    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
   170	  fi
   171	  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
   172	  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   173	    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   174	  else
   175	    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   176	  fi
   177	  return 0
   178	}
   179	
   180	# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
   181	# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
   182	_loa_pl_load() {
   183	  _loa_pl_paths
   184	  _loa_pl_id
   185	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
   186	    return 0
   187	  fi
   188	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
   189	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
   190	    local j
   191	    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
   192	        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
   193	    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
   194	      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
   195	      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   196	      return 0
   197	    fi
   198	  fi
   199	  _loa_pl_build || return 1
   200	  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   201	  _loa_pl_write_cache
   202	  return 0
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
   206	_loa_pl_live() {
   207	  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
   208	  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   209	    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
   210	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   211	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   212	      return 0
   213	    fi
   214	  fi
   215	  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   216	  return 0
   217	}
   218	
   219	loa_knob() {
   220	  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
   221	  key="${path#.}"
   222	  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
   223	    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
   224	    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   225	    return 2
   226	  fi
   227	  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
   228	  _loa_pl_paths
   229	  _loa_pl_id
   230	  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
   231	     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   232	    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
   233	          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
   234	            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   235	               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   236	             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
   237	          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
   238	    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   239	      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   240	      return 0
   241	    fi
   242	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
   243	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   244	      return 0
   245	    fi
   246	  fi
   247	  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
   248	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   249	    return 0
   250	  fi
   251	  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
   252	        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   253	          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   254	        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
   255	  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   256	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   257	    return 0
   258	  fi
   259	  printf '%s\n' "$v"
   260	  return 0
   261	}
   262	
   263	loa_profile() {
   264	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   265	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
   266	  else
   267	    echo standard
   268	  fi
   269	  return 0
   270	}
   271	
   272	loa_profile_source() {
   273	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   274	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
   275	  else
   276	    echo default
   277	  fi
   278	  return 0
   279	}
   280	
   281	loa_profile_overrides() {
   282	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   283	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
   284	  fi
   285	  return 0
   286	}
   287	
   288	loa_effective_json() {
   289	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   290	    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
   291	  else
   292	    echo '{}'
   293	  fi
   294	  return 0
   295	}
   296	
   297	if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
   298	  export LC_ALL=C
   299	  case "${1:-}" in
   300	    profile)   loa_profile ;;
   301	    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
   302	    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
   303	               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
   304	    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
   305	    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
   306	    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
   307	  esac
   308	fi
