1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# implement-gate.sh — Dual-mode compliance hook for App Zone writes (FR-7)
4	# =============================================================================
5	# Checks whether Write/Edit to App Zone files occurs within an active
6	# /implement or /bug skill invocation.
7	#
8	# Modes (cycle-129 D-4.1, DEC-0163; .loa.config.yaml implement_gate.mode):
9	#   ask (default; unset or any other value): an unsanctioned App-Zone write asks,
10	#       exactly as before, and now logs one row (decision "ask").
11	#   telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one row (action "telemetry",
12	#       decision "outside_run") and is allowed silently.
13	#   deny: an unsanctioned App-Zone write is DENIED when the run position is
14	#       known: .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and its derived_at is within
15	#       run_mode.stale_hours (12). The gate is a fence only in this mode. An
16	#       unknown position (cache missing, not derived, stale or unparseable)
17	#       falls back to ask (decision "unknown_position"), never to allow.
18	# Sanction (any mode; first match wins; one row each, action "allow"):
19	#   sanctioned_run    — the heuristic below: a fresh RUNNING cache, and its
20	#                       derived_at (when present) within run_mode.stale_hours
21	#   sanctioned_marker — .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint,
22	#                       started_at} with started_at within two hours (written by
23	#                       `run-checkpoint.sh mark`, removed by `unmark`); a stale or
24	#                       malformed marker logs decision "stale_marker" and does not sanction
25	#   override          — LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the hook's environment
26	# Rows go to .run/audit.jsonl as {ts, hook: "implement-gate", action, decision,
27	# mode, path} with path control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes; LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
28	# adds replay: true to every row this gate writes (DEC-0167).
29	#
30	# Claims modifier (implement_gate.claims: authoritative; the legacy
31	# implement_gate.mode: authoritative means mode ask + claims authoritative):
32	#   reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin. The PreToolUse
33	#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
34	#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this modifier.
35	#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
36	#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
37	#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
38	#      non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny with a known position and no
39	#      sanction, is denied) and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
40	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
41	#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask"/"deny" for a non-implementation
42	#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
43	#
44	# `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode [CONFIG]` prints the effective mode (and the
45	# claims modifier) without reading stdin — the /loa Gate line.
46	#
47	# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
48	# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
49	# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
50	#
51	# Failure mode: FAIL-ASK for App Zone writes (not fail-open). A payload jq cannot
52	# parse (or no jq), or a file_path that cannot be canonicalised, asks too (run-2
53	# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
54	# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
55	# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
56	# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
57	# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location
58	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
59	# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
60	# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
61	# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl,
62	# .run/implement-active.json or .loa.config.yaml asks in every mode and under
63	# every sanction, and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
64	# Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.
65	#
66	# Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent
67	# exit 0 with empty stdout; ask = exit 0 with
68	#   {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}
69	# deny = the same shape with "permissionDecision":"deny".
70	# A top-level "decision" accepts approve|block only, so "ask" never goes there.
71	# file_path and active_skill reach stderr only through strip_controls (n21;
72	# run-2 findings 3/12; run-3 finding 5): cut to 256 bytes without splitting a
73	# character, then C0 and DEL, UTF-8 C1 controls and the Unicode format/bidi/tag
74	# code points are removed to a fixed point. Audit rows record the RAW values cut
75	# the same way and written with jq -a, so every non-ASCII code point is \uXXXX:
76	# faithful (implement+U+200B logs as implement\u200b) and terminal-safe (run-3 finding 4).
77	#
78	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — hook must never crash-block.
79	# Parse/read errors on App Zone writes → ask (not allow).
80	#
81	# Part of cycle-049/050: Upstream Platform Alignment (FR-7)
82	# Red Team findings addressed: ATK-005 (state tampering), ATK-006 (fail-open),
83	#   ATK-007 (prompt injection via file path)
84	# Sprint-108 T4.4: Dual-mode (authoritative + heuristic)
85	# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization
86	# =============================================================================
87	
88	# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
89	input=""
90	if [[ "${1:-}" != "--effective-mode" ]]; then
91	    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
92	fi
93	
94	# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
95	# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
96	emit_ask() {
97	    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
98	        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
99	    else
100	        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
101	    fi
102	}
103	
104	# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
105	# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
106	# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
107	# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
108	# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
109	_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
110	_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
111	    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
112	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
113	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
114	    done
115	    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
116	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
117	    done
118	    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
119	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
120	    done
121	    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
122	        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
123	    done
124	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
125	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
126	    done
127	    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
128	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
129	    done
130	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
131	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
132	    done
133	}
134	
135	# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
136	# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
137	# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
138	cut_utf8_256() {
139	    local LC_ALL=C
140	    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
141	    _c_n=${#_c_s}
142	    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
143	        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
144	        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
145	        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
146	        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
147	        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
148	        fi
149	        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
150	        return 0
151	    done
152	    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
153	}
154	
155	# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
156	# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
157	# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
158	strip_controls() {
159	    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq
160	    cut_utf8_256 s "$1"
161	    s=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')
162	    (( ${#_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]} )) || _ig_strip_seqs_init
163	    while :; do
164	        prev=$s
165	        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done
166	        [[ "$s" == "$prev" ]] && break
167	    done
168	    printf '%s' "$s"
169	}
170	
171	# The root never follows the process cwd, which follows Claude's `cd` (sprint-250 audit MED-001): PROJECT_ROOT, then
172	# the harness's CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (it stays at the session's project root), then this script's own location
173	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/)
174	PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)}}"
175	RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.run}"
176	FEATURES_FILE="$RUN_DIR/platform-features.json"
177	
178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
179	# Mode and claims (cycle-129 D-4.1): one yq call, read only when a decision
180	# needs it. Unset, unreadable or unknown values are ask; the legacy
181	# mode: authoritative is ask + claims: authoritative. run_mode.stale_hours
182	# bounds derived_at (positive integer, default 12).
183	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
184	gate_mode="ask"
185	gate_claims="plain"
186	gate_stale_hours=12
187	load_gate_config() {
188	    local cfg="${1:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml}" raw m c s
189	    command -v yq &>/dev/null && command -v jq &>/dev/null && [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || return 0
190	    # mikefarah yq v4 first; the python yq wrapper (jq syntax, JSON out) second
191	    raw=$(yq -o json -I 0 '{"m": .implement_gate.mode, "c": .implement_gate.claims, "s": .run_mode.stale_hours}' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null) \
192	        || raw=$(yq -c '{"m": .implement_gate.mode, "c": .implement_gate.claims, "s": .run_mode.stale_hours}' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null) \
193	        || return 0
194	    m=$(jq -r '.m | strings' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || m=""
195	    c=$(jq -r '.c | strings' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || c=""
196	    s=$(jq -r '.s | numbers | tostring' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || s=""
197	    case "$m" in
198	        ask|telemetry|deny) gate_mode="$m" ;;
199	        authoritative) gate_claims="authoritative" ;;
200	    esac
201	    [[ "$c" == "authoritative" ]] && gate_claims="authoritative"
202	    if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] && (( 10#$s > 0 && 10#$s <= 8760 )); then gate_stale_hours=$(( 10#$s )); fi
203	    return 0
204	}
205	
206	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--effective-mode" ]]; then
207	    load_gate_config "${2:-}"
208	    if [[ "$gate_claims" == "authoritative" ]]; then echo "$gate_mode (claims: authoritative)"; else echo "$gate_mode"; fi
209	    exit 0
210	fi
211	
212	# Row helpers: LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 marks every row this gate writes (DEC-0167)
213	_ig_replay_json='{}'
214	[[ "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" == "1" ]] && _ig_replay_json='{"replay":true}'
215	
216	# Evidence recorder: lead session only (no teammate role, no subagent agent_id), once, atomic.
217	if [[ -z "${LOA_TEAM_MEMBER:-}" && -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] \
218	    && jq -e '(.tool_input.active_skill // "") != "" and (.agent_id // "") == ""' <<<"$input" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
219	    && ! jq -e '.active_skill_seen_at' "$FEATURES_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
220	    _ig_base=$(jq -c 'select(type == "object")' "$FEATURES_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
221	    _ig_tmp=$(mktemp "$RUN_DIR/.platform-features.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) && {
222	        jq -nc --argjson b "${_ig_base:-{\}}" --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
223	            '$b + {active_skill_available: false, active_skill_seen_at: $ts, active_skill_source: "tool_input"}' > "$_ig_tmp" 2>/dev/null \
224	            && mv -f "$_ig_tmp" "$FEATURES_FILE" 2>/dev/null
225	        rm -f "$_ig_tmp" 2>/dev/null
226	    }
227	fi
228	
229	# No jq, or a payload jq cannot parse: the write cannot be evaluated, so ask (run-2 finding 5)
230	if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null || ! jq -e . <<<"$input" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
231	    echo "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input (jq missing or payload unparsable)." >&2

259	# T4.5: Path normalization — canonicalise both sides, then take file_path
260	# relative to the project root (run-2 finding 1). A textual prefix test let
261	# /proc/self/cwd/src/x, //ROOT/src/x, ROOT/../<name>/src/x or a symlinked root
262	# reach an App-Zone file unseen. Two forms are tested and either one matching
263	# counts (run-3 finding 1): the PHYSICAL form follows symlinks (realpath -m,
264	# else readlink -f) against pwd -P of the root; the LOGICAL form keeps them

266	# src/ that is itself a symlink out of the root still asks. A relative path
267	# resolves from the payload's cwd when it carries one (the harness resolves it
268	# there and cwd follows `cd` in the Bash tool), else from PROJECT_ROOT (run-3

270	# names never count (e.g., /home/user/src-projects/loa/grimoires/file.md is not src/*).
271	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
272	# Lexical normaliser for an absolute path: drops empty and . components, resolves .. textually, follows no symlink
273	_ig_lexical_norm() {
274	    local rest=$1 part
275	    local -a out=()
276	    while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
277	        part=${rest%%/*}
278	        if [[ "$rest" == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=""; fi

280	            ''|.) ;;
281	            ..) (( ${#out[@]} )) && unset 'out[${#out[@]}-1]' ;;

286	    printf '/%s' "${out[*]}"

385	# One decision row per App-Zone write: {ts, hook, action, decision, mode, path}; path is the display copy

417	                --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
418	                --arg skill "$audit_skill" \

454	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
455	# Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?

457	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
458	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
459	# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
460	_ig_fresh() {
461	    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
462	    local now last_epoch
463	    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
464	    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
465	        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""

473	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $2 parses, is at most $1 seconds old and at most 300 s ahead (clock skew);
474	# jq's fromdateiso8601 keeps it portable (no GNU date -d). Fractional seconds are dropped first

478	        '($t | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $e | $e != null and (now - $e) <= $w and ($e - now) <= 300' \

544	# The implementing skills' marker (run-checkpoint.sh mark): 0 fresh and well-formed, 1 absent, 2 stale or malformed
545	check_implement_marker() {

610	    exit 0
611	fi
612	
613	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
614	# Decision

620	fi
621	
622	case "$gate_mode" in
623	    telemetry)

625	        log_gate_row telemetry outside_run
626	        exit 0
627	        ;;
628	    deny)
629	        if read_position; then
630	            echo "[GATE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' denied: no active implementation run (derived position: $position_state)." >&2
631	            log_gate_row deny deny
632	            emit_deny "$(deny_reason)"
633	            exit 0
634	        fi
635	        # Unknown position: ask, never allow
636	        echo "[GATE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' outside an active run; run position unknown ($position_why), asking instead of denying." >&2
637	        log_gate_row ask unknown_position
638	        emit_ask "[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation; run position unknown ($position_why). Verify this is intentional."
639	        exit 0
640	        ;;

642	        # No active implementation detected — ADVISORY ask (unchanged), now counted
643	        echo "[ADVISORY] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected outside active /implement or /bug." >&2

    18	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every

compliance_mode="heuristic"
if command -v yq &>/dev/null && [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
    configured_mode=$(yq '.implement_gate.mode // ""' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" 2>/dev/null) || configured_mode=""
    [[ "${configured_mode//\"/}" == "authoritative" ]] && compliance_mode="authoritative"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authoritative mode: read active_skill from hook input
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$compliance_mode" == "authoritative" ]]; then
    active_skill=$(jq -j '.tool_input.active_skill // empty' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null && printf x) || active_skill="x"
    active_skill=${active_skill%x}

    if [[ -n "$active_skill" ]]; then
        safe_skill=$(strip_controls "$active_skill")
        cut_utf8_256 audit_skill "$active_skill"
        # One model_signal row per invocation that carries a claim; the harness never sets the field,
        # so a row means a model wrote it (run-2 finding 6). The row holds the raw claim, ASCII-escaped (run-3 finding 4)
        log_model_signal() {
            jq -nca \
                --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
                --arg skill "$audit_skill" \
                --arg path "$audit_file_path" \
                --arg decision "$1" \
                '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.mode.model_signal", mode: "authoritative", active_skill: $skill, file_path: $path, decision: $decision}' \
                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
        }
        case "$active_skill" in
            implement|/implement|bug|/bug|run|/run|simstim|/simstim)
                # Tighten-only (n17/n18): a model-authored implementation claim never
                # allows by itself — log it, then fall through to the heuristic check below
                log_model_signal heuristic
                ;;
            *)
                # Non-implementation skill — log the model signal and ask
                echo "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected during /$safe_skill (not an implementation skill)." >&2
                log_model_signal ask
                emit_ask "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write outside implementation skill. Verify this is intentional."
                exit 0
                ;;
        esac
    else
        # active_skill field absent despite authoritative mode — fall back to heuristic
        # Log the downgrade
        log_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null) || log_ts="unknown"
        if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
            jq -nc \
                --arg ts "$log_ts" \
                --arg from "authoritative" \
                --arg to "heuristic" \
                --arg reason "active_skill field absent in hook input" \
                '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.mode.fallback", from_mode: $from, to_mode: $to, reason: $reason}' \
                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
        else
            echo "{\"timestamp\":\"$log_ts\",\"event\":\"compliance.mode.fallback\",\"from_mode\":\"authoritative\",\"to_mode\":\"heuristic\",\"reason\":\"active_skill field absent in hook input\"}" \
                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    fi
    # Fall through to heuristic check below
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?
# Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json, .run/simstim-state.json, .run/state.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
_ig_fresh() {
    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
    local now last_epoch
    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
    else
        last_epoch=$(date -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -jf '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
    fi
    [[ "$last_epoch" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    (( last_epoch > 0 && now - last_epoch <= 86400 && last_epoch - now <= 86400 ))
}

check_implementation_active() {
    # Check sprint-plan state
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
        local state plan_id last_activity
        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true

        # Integrity: must have plan_id
        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi

        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
        fi

        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
        local phase simstim_activity
        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
        local run_state run_activity
        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision: allow or ask
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if check_implementation_active; then
    # Implementation is active — allow the write
    exit 0
else
    # No active implementation detected — ADVISORY ask
    echo "[ADVISORY] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected outside active /implement or /bug." >&2
    echo "No RUNNING state found in .run/ state files. This may bypass review gates." >&2
    echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation. Verify this is intentional."}}'
    exit 0
fi

#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
  done <<<"$rows"

  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
  rounds="[]"
  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
  fi
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")

  local facts report
  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
    {sprints: $s,
     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
       notes: ([
         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
       ]),
       sprints: $f.sprints,
       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
       written: false}')

  if (( write )); then
    local why=""
    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
    fi
    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
    else
      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
    fi
  fi

  if (( json )); then
    jq . <<<"$report"
  else
    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_record_round() {
  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  local p th ts now out trip
  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
    return 0
  fi
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
        else null end ) as $trip
    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"

+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
+# is not optional.
+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$o_heading"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local tmp="${file}.prune-tmp" rc=0
+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
+    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }
+    state == "" && $0 == heading { state = "head"; n = 0; buf[++n] = $0; next }
+    state == "head" {
+      if (index($0, start)) { state = "skip"; n = 0; next }
+      if ($0 ~ /^\|/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) { buf[++n] = $0; next }
+      flush(); state = ""; print; next
+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in
+      3) log "ERROR: ${file}: no end marker for optional section '${section}'" ;;
+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  verbose "Pruned empty optional section ${section} (${heading}) from ${file}"
+}

log "WARNING: Target file not found: $s_target, skipping"
      continue
    fi

    target_sections["$s_target"]+="${s_name} "
    section_data["$s_name"]="${s_target}|${s_template}|${s_filter}"
  done

  if [[ ${#target_sections[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    log "No sections to generate"
    return 0
  fi

  # Phase 1: Create staged copies
  declare -A staged_files
  trap 'for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done' EXIT

  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp "${target}.constraint-XXXXXX")
    cp "$target" "$tmp"
    staged_files["$target"]="$tmp"
  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi
    done
  done

  # Phase 3: Diff or commit
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
      log "Diff for ${target}:"
      diff -u "$target" "${staged_files[$target]}" || true
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    trap - EXIT
    return 0
  fi

  # Commit with rollback
  declare -A backup_files
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local bak="${target}.constraint-bak"
    cp "$target" "$bak"
    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"
  done

  local commit_failed=false
  local committed=()

Documented accepted bypass classes (cycle-111 SDD §11): newline statement separators, subshell wrapping (`bash -c '...'` quoted-differently, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing WHERE, python scripts loaded from disk, jq absent from PATH. +### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)
+
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.
+

A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:

This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. #!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# implement-gate.bats — cycle-126 Sprint 4 Task 4.4 (SDD D-4.4, Flatline SKP-008)
#
# The PreToolUse stdin carries no harness-set skill signal
# (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks lists session_id, transcript_path,
# cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id,
# and agent_id/agent_type inside a subagent). tool_input is model-authored,
# so `tool_input.active_skill` is evidence at most:
#   - the recorder writes active_skill_seen_at once, from the lead session only
#   - nothing in .run/ flips the gate; only `implement_gate.mode: authoritative`
#     in .loa.config.yaml does, and the key stays undocumented
#   - detect-platform-features.sh never reports the flag true on its own
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0   # `run -1 grep`: a bare `! grep` cannot fail, and only "no match" (exit 1) passes — a missing file (exit 2) fails (sprint-250 review run 2, #10)
    REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    GATE="$REPO/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh"
    DETECT="$REPO/.claude/scripts/detect-platform-features.sh"
    FIX="$REPO/tests/fixtures/pretooluse-payloads"
    ROOT="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
    mkdir -p "$ROOT/.run"
    unset LOA_TEAM_MEMBER CLAUDE_ACTIVE_SKILL_AVAILABLE
}

payload() { sed "s#__ROOT__#$ROOT#g" "$FIX/$1"; }

gate_with() {
    local fixture="$1"
    payload "$fixture" > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
    run --separate-stderr bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
}

# Claude Code PreToolUse contract: "ask" is only valid as hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; a top-level
# "decision" takes approve|block only (sprint-250 audit n20). Allow = silent exit 0 with empty stdout.
decision() {
    if [[ -z "$output" ]]; then echo allow
    elif jq -e '(has("decision") | not) and .hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName == "PreToolUse"
                and .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision == "ask"
                and (.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason | type == "string" and length > 0)' <<<"$output" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ask
    else echo "invalid:$output"; fi
}

opt_in() { printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"; }

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
     5	# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
     6	# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
     7	# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
     8	# All files live in a temp dir.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    13	  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
    14	  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
    16	  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
    17	  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
    18	  S="$T/.run/state.json"
    19	  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
    20	}
    21	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    22	
    23	# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
    24	fb() {
    25	  local prose
    26	  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
    27	    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    28	  else
    29	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
    30	  fi
    31	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
    32	    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
    33	}
    34	
    35	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
    36	
    37	breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
    38	  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
    39	          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
    40	                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
    41	          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
    42	}
    43	
    44	rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
    45	
    46	@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
    47	  breaker
    48	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
    49	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    50	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    51	  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
    52	  local want
    53	  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
    54	  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
    55	  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
    56	  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
    57	}
    58	
    59	@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
    60	  breaker
    61	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
    62	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    63	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    64	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
    65	  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
    66	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2
    67	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    68	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    69	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 1 ]
    70	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")" != "$h1" ]
    71	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$B")" = 3 ]
    72	}
    73	
    74	@test "RCR-3 no_progress counts consecutive rounds whose counts are unchanged and resets when they change" {

**cycle-122 additions**: `FR-MERGE-2` blocks manual `git tag` creation (listing/inspect/delete forms allowed; audited override `LOA_ALLOW_GIT_TAG=1`) — C-MERGE-002's mechanical twin. `FR-1.2b` blocks output-swallowed `git stash push/pop/apply` (`| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null` — the issue #555 silent-data-loss shapes); remedy: `stash_with_guard`. `FR-SZ2` blocks direct Bash writes into `.claude/` (redirect/tee/copy/sed-i/rm shapes; `.claude/overrides/` + `.claude/cache/` excluded) unless the bounded framework-dev marker (`.run/zone-guard-authorization.json`, same validation as zone-write-guard) or `LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE=1` authorizes — closing the single-agent System-Zone Bash gap. Same accepted-bypass classes as their parents (fence, not boundary).

**cycle-128 additions**: `SP-1` keeps spike content out of every other branch, and FR-1.1 lets a fully pushed spike branch with an operator-decided ledger row be deleted. Both are described, with their accepted misses, under [Decision surfaces](#decision-surfaces-cycle-128).

A separate script-level runtime layer (`dcg-exec.sh` + `destructive-command-guard.sh`, pattern packs for core/database/docker/kubernetes) validates commands executed by Loa scripts with configurable BLOCK/WARN/ALLOW actions — invocation and pack details live in those scripts' headers.

**Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111)**: this hook is a fence against routine destructive mistakes by autonomous agents — NOT a hardened security boundary. Documented accepted bypass classes (cycle-111 SDD §11): newline statement separators, subshell wrapping (`bash -c '...'` quoted-differently, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing WHERE, python scripts loaded from disk, jq absent from PATH. ERE flavor: GNU/BSD-compatible extensions (`\s`, `\b`), NOT strict POSIX. Latency budget: p95 < 80ms across 100 invocations (bash startup + jq + 13 grep passes).

### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)

Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:

- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.

**Accepted false positives (quote-blindness residue, cycle-120 C-D3)**: the inert-carrier scrub redacts a known data carrier's value (git commit `-m`, `br`/`bd -d`, `gh … create --body/--title`, `echo`/`printf`) only when the value holds **neither `$(` nor a backtick**. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:

- **Case A — a `$(…)` command-substitution inside a carrier value** (e.g. a multi-line commit body wrapped in `$(cat <<'EOF' … find -exec rm -rf … EOF)`). The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. Backtick command-substitution itself remains the separately-tracked, uncaught pre-existing gap (bd-bdb-backtick-bypass).

# run-mode Sprint Plan Execution Loop (`/run sprint-plan`)

## Sprint Discovery

Try each source in priority order; use the first that returns non-empty:

1. **Priority 1 — `sprint.md` sections**: `grep -E "^## Sprint [0-9]+:" grimoires/loa/sprint.md | sed 's/## Sprint \([0-9]*\):.*/sprint-\1/' | sort -t'-' -k2 -n`.

3. **Priority 3 — a2a directories**: `find grimoires/loa/a2a -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "sprint-*" | sed 's|.*/||' | sort -t'-' -k2 -n`.

  local errors=0

  # Check top-level required fields
  if ! jq -e '.version and .constraints' "$REGISTRY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "Missing required top-level fields (version, constraints)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Check version pattern
  local version
  version=$(jq -r '.version' "$REGISTRY")
  if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    fail "Invalid version format: $version"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check each constraint has required fields
  local missing
  missing=$(jq -r '
    [.constraints[] | select(
      (.id | not) or (.name | not) or (.category | not) or
      (.rule_type | not) or (.text | not) or (.why | not) or
      (.layers | not) or (.severity | not)
    ) | .id // "UNKNOWN"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
    fail "Constraints missing required fields: $missing"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check ID pattern
  local bad_ids
  bad_ids=$(jq -r '[.constraints[] | select(.id | test("^C-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3}$") | not) | .id] | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_ids" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid constraint IDs: $bad_ids"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check category enum
  local bad_cats
  bad_cats=$(jq -r '
    ["process","git_safety","beads","danger_level","flatline","guardrails","phase_sequencing","eval","bridge","merge","agent_teams","permission"] as $valid |
    [.constraints[] | select(.category | IN($valid[]) | not) | "\(.id): \(.category)"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_cats" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid categories: $bad_cats"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check rule_type enum
  local bad_types
  bad_types=$(jq -r '
    ["NEVER","ALWAYS","WHEN","MUST","SHOULD","MAY"] as $valid |
    [.constraints[] | select(.rule_type | IN($valid[]) | not) | "\(.id): \(.rule_type)"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -n "$bad_types" ]]; then
    fail "Invalid rule_types: $bad_types"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  if [[ "$errors" -eq 0 ]]; then
    pass "Schema validation passed (jq fallback)"

  return $((errors > 0 ? 1 : 0))

    local s_name s_target s_template s_filter
    IFS='|' read -r s_name s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$entry"

    if [[ ! -f "$s_target" ]]; then
      verbose "Skipping freshness for $s_name: target not found"
      continue
    fi

    # Check if markers exist in target
    if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${s_name}" "$s_target" 2>/dev/null; then
      verbose "Skipping freshness for $s_name: no markers in $s_target"
      continue
    fi

    # Extract stored hash from start marker
    local stored_hash
    stored_hash=$(grep "@constraint-generated: start ${s_name}" "$s_target" | sed -n 's/.*hash:\([a-f0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)

    if [[ -z "$stored_hash" ]]; then
      warn "No hash found in marker for section '$s_name' in $s_target"
      continue
    fi

    # Regenerate content
    local template_file="${TEMPLATE_DIR}/${s_template}"
    if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
      fail "Template not found: $template_file"
      stale=$((stale + 1))
      continue
    fi

    local expected_content
    expected_content=$(jq -r "$s_filter" "$REGISTRY" | jq -r -f "$template_file")

    local expected_hash
    expected_hash=$(compute_section_hash "$expected_content")

    if [[ "$stored_hash" != "$expected_hash" ]]; then
      fail "STALE: Section '$s_name' in $s_target (stored: $stored_hash, expected: $expected_hash)"
      stale=$((stale + 1))
    else
      pass "Section '$s_name' in $s_target is fresh"
    fi
  done

  return $((stale > 0 ? 1 : 0))
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
4	# DEC-0141).
5	#
6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
8	# PER TASK:
9	#
10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
23	#
24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
29	#
30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
34	# file is not written through.
35	#
36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
40	#
41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
44	# full each time and those caches are gone.
45	
46	set -uo pipefail
47	umask 077
48	export LC_ALL=C
49	
50	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
51	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
52	[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
53	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
54	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
55	DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
56	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
57	DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
58	STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
59	SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
60	LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
61	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
62	CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
63	KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
64	[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20
65	
66	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
67	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
68	[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0
69	
70	# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
71	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
72	source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
73	if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
74	switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
75	case "$switch" in
76	    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
77	esac
78	THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
79	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
80	THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))
81	
82	# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
83	payload="$(cat)"
84	[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
85	fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
86	    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
87	    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
88	            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
89	            else 1 end;
90	    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
91	    select(type == "object") |
92	    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
93	    ([($tn | tojson),
94	      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
95	       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
96	       else 0 end | tostring),
97	      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
98	      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
99	      (now | todate)] | .[])
100	' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
101	{
102	    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
103	    IFS= read -r LINES
104	    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
105	    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
106	    IFS= read -r TS
107	} <<< "$fields"
108	case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
109	    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
110	    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
111	    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
112	    *) exit 0 ;;
113	esac
114	[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
115	[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0
116	
117	# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
118	_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
119	    local s
120	    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
121	    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
122	    printf '%s' "$s"
123	}
124	payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
125	SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
126	[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
127	SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
128	
129	task_raw=""
130	if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
131	    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
132	        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
133	                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
134	        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
135	fi
136	KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
137	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
138	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
139	
140	# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
141	if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
142	    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
143	    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
144	        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
145	                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
146	    fi
147	fi
148	
149	# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
150	[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
151	[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
152	TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
153	[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
154	
155	PRIOR=0
156	if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
157	    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
158	    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
159	    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
160	fi
161	RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
162	
163	printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
164	    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
165	
166	# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
167	# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
168	n=0
169	while IFS= read -r old; do
170	    n=$((n + 1))
171	    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
172	        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
173	    fi
174	done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)
175	
176	# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
177	OVER=false
178	(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
179	sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
180	[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
181	if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
182	    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
183	    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
184	            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
185	        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
186	    else
187	        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
188	    fi
189	fi
190	
191	# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
192	if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
193	    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2
194	
195	    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
196	        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
197	        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
198	        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
199	    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
200	    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
201	    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
202	    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
203	    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
204	        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
205	        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
206	fi
207	
208	exit 0

    fi

  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else

  fi
  return 0
}

    12	#   reaches the agent. This surface is only useful IN CONTEXT, so every ENABLED

    17	#   the same way. The DISABLED path emits nothing at all.

    26	#   - When ENABLED and healthy: emit a compact symptom -> KF table to STDOUT,
    27	#     exit 0.

    33	# =============================================================================
    34	set -uo pipefail
    35	
    36	HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# Issue #961 K-1 — Karpathy surgical-diff hook
# =============================================================================
# Pins the contract for .claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:
# fires `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the
# session diff accumulator exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task`,
# while remaining non-blocking (always exits 0) per v1 invariant.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$REPO_ROOT/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    [[ -x "$HOOK" ]] || skip "hook not executable"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"

    TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
    # cycle-129 D-4.3: per-task state under KARPATHY_STATE_DIR; with no run in
    # progress (empty LOA_RUN_DIR) the key is the session id.
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$TMP_DIR/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$TMP_DIR/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$TMP_DIR/legacy-task-state.jsonl"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$TMP_DIR/run"
    export LOA_SESSION_ID="test-session"
    KARPATHY_TASK_STATE="$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/test-session.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$TMP_DIR/trajectory"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$TMP_DIR/config.yaml"

    # Default test config — surgical_diff_warning on, threshold deliberately
    # tiny so we can trip it with a few small Write calls.
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: true
  diff_lines_per_task: 5
  enforce: warn
EOF
}

teardown() {
    rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"
}

_write_input() {
    local content="$1"
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" '{tool_name:"Write", tool_input:{file_path:"/tmp/x.txt", content:$c}}'
}

_edit_input() {
    local new="$1"
    jq -nc --arg n "$new" '{tool_name:"Edit", tool_input:{file_path:"/tmp/x.txt", old_string:"", new_string:$n}}'
}
